title: Localization with Portable Object (PO) Files
description: Use PO files as a human-readable, collaboration-friendly alternative to .resx resource files for ASP.NET Core localization.

terms.definition: A plain-text localization file using the gettext format. Stores msgid (source string) and msgstr (translated string) pairs. Human-readable and easy for translators to edit.
A widely used internationalization framework. PO files are its native format, supported by many translation tools like Poedit.
Handling different grammatical forms for different quantities — e.g., '1 item' vs '5 items'. PO files support msgid_plural for this.
A context prefix in a PO file entry that limits when a translation is applied — useful when the same word means different things in different views.
A NuGet package that adds AddPortableObjectLocalization() to ASP.NET Core's service collection, enabling PO file support.

data.text: What Are PO Files?

Portable Object (PO) files are plain-text files that follow the gettext format. Each entry maps an original (untranslated) string to its translation. They are an alternative to `.resx` files with some practical advantages:

data.title: Advantages of PO files
items: Plain text — no binary compilation required, easy to version-control and diff.
Built-in pluralization support (msgid_plural) for languages with complex plural rules.
Work seamlessly with popular translation tools like Poedit, Transifex, and Weblate.
Human-readable format that translators can work with directly.

data.title: When to choose PO files over .resx
data.text: Use PO files when you have a team of translators, need pluralization support, or prefer a non-XML format. Use .resx files for simpler projects or when you rely on Visual Studio's built-in resource editor.
Step 1 — Install the Package
Add the OrchardCore.Localization.Core NuGet package to your project:

data.title: Install via .NET CLI
data.content: Run this command in the project directory to add PO file localization support.

data.text: Step 2 — Configure Services in Program.cs
Register PO file localization alongside your MVC services. The key addition is `AddPortableObjectLocalization()`, which tells ASP.NET Core to look for `.po` files instead of `.resx` files.

data.title: Program.cs — PO file configuration
data.content: Configure three supported cultures and register PO localization alongside MVC view localization.

data.title: PO file placement
data.text: Place .po files in the same folder as the controller or view they localize. For HomeController, use fr.po and es.po in the Controllers/ folder. For Index.cshtml, use fr.po and es.po in Views/Home/.
Step 3 — Create PO Files
PO files are plain-text. Create one file per culture. Each entry has a `msgid` (source string) and a `msgstr` (translated string):

data.title: fr.po — French translations
data.content: A minimal French PO file with one translated string and the required metadata header.
data.code:
# French translations for the project.
# Copyright (C) 2024
#
msgid ""
msgstr ""
"Project-Id-Version: MyApp 1.0\n"
"Language: fr\n"
"MIME-Version: 1.0\n"
"Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8\n"
"Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit\n"

#: Controllers/HomeController.cs:15
msgid "Application submitted successfully"
msgstr "Demande soumise avec succès"

#: Views/Home/Index.cshtml:3
msgid "Job Application"
msgstr "Demande d'emploi"

#: Views/Home/Index.cshtml:20
msgid "Submit Application"
msgstr "Soumettre la candidature"

data.title: es.po — Spanish translations
data.content: A minimal Spanish PO file with the same keys translated to Spanish.
data.code:
# Spanish translations for the project.
# Copyright (C) 2024
#
msgid ""
msgstr ""
"Project-Id-Version: MyApp 1.0\n"
"Language: es\n"
"MIME-Version: 1.0\n"
"Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8\n"
"Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit\n"

#: Controllers/HomeController.cs:15
msgid "Application submitted successfully"
msgstr "Solicitud enviada con éxito"

#: Views/Home/Index.cshtml:3
msgid "Job Application"
msgstr "Solicitud de empleo"

#: Views/Home/Index.cshtml:20
msgid "Submit Application"
msgstr "Enviar solicitud"

data.title: PO file header format
data.text: The msgstr "" entry at the top is the file header. It must contain Language, Content-Type (charset=UTF-8), and Content-Transfer-Encoding. Without this header, ASP.NET Core will not recognize the file.
Step 4 — Read PO Strings in a Controller
Using PO files in a controller is identical to using resource files — inject `IStringLocalizer<T>` and call the indexer:

data.title: Controllers/HomeController.cs
data.content: IStringLocalizer works the same way regardless of whether you use .resx or .po files.

data.text: Step 5 — Read PO Strings in a Razor View
Inject `IViewLocalizer` in your Razor view to translate static text. The view looks for a `.po` file in the same directory:

data.title: Views/Home/Index.cshtml
data.content: Inject IViewLocalizer and use it to localize headings, labels, and button text.

data.text: Step 6 — Pluralization in PO Files

Not all languages follow English pluralization rules. French has two plural forms (one and more-than-one), while languages like Russian or Arabic have six. PO files handle this with `msgid_plural` and indexed `msgstr[n]`:

data.title: fr.po — plural form example
data.content: msgid_plural provides the plural template, and msgstr[0], msgstr[1], etc. provide each plural form.
data.code:
# French has 2 plural forms: n=0 (one) and n>0 (many)

msgid "There is one item in your cart."
msgid_plural "There are {0} items in your cart."
msgstr[0] "Il y a un article dans votre panier."
msgstr[1] "Il y a {0} articles dans votre panier."

data.title: Razor view — using Localizer.Plural()
data.content: Call the Plural method with the count, singular form, and plural form.

data.title: Plural forms are language-specific
data.text: French uses 2 forms (n=0 and n>0). Arabic uses 6 forms (n=0, n=1, n=2, n=3-10, n=11-99, n=100+). Poedit and most PO editors handle plural formula rules automatically based on the Language header.
Step 7 — Use msgctxt for Context-Scoped Translations
Sometimes the same English word needs different translations in different parts of your app. `msgctxt` scopes a translation to a specific view or controller:

data.title: fr.po — context-scoped entries
data.content: The same English word 'Close' gets a different French translation depending on the view context.
data.code:
# In Views/Products/Index.cshtml — 'Close' as a button label
msgctxt "Views.Products.Index"
msgid "Close"
msgstr "Fermer"

# In Views/Shared/_Modal.cshtml — 'Close' as a dismiss action
msgctxt "Views.Shared._Modal"
msgid "Close"
msgstr "Fermer la fenêtre"

data.text: PO File Structure Reference

data.caption: How ASP.NET Core resolves a PO file lookup for a view
data.definition:
flowchart LR
    A[Razor View calls Localizer["Submit"]] --> B[IViewLocalizer]
    B --> C{Current Culture = fr?}
    C -->|yes| D[Look in Views/Home/Index.fr.po]
    C -->|no| E[Look in Views/Home/Index.es.po]
    D --> F{msgid "Submit" found?}
    E --> F
    F -->|yes| G[Return msgstr translation]
    F -->|no| H[Return original msgid as fallback]
    G --> I[Rendered HTML]
    H --> I

cards.title: .resx (Resource Files)
cards.description: XML-based files compiled into the assembly. Native to .NET and Visual Studio.
cons: XML is verbose and hard to diff

cards.title: PO (Portable Object) Files
cards.description: Plain-text gettext format. Human-readable and translator-friendly via tools like Poedit.
pros: Plain text — easy to version control

data.title: Exercise: Pluralize a Shopping Cart Message
data.description: Use PO file pluralization to show the correct item count message in French and Spanish.
steps: Add a ShoppingCart.cshtml view to your project.
In the PO setup you already have, add these plural entries to fr.po: msgid 'You have 0 items.' / msgid_plural 'You have {0} items.' with two msgstr entries for French.
Add the same entries to es.po for Spanish.
In the ShoppingCart view, inject IViewLocalizer and call Localizer.Plural(count, "You have 0 items.", "You have {0} items.") for counts of 0, 1, and 5.
Run the app with ?culture=fr and verify each count shows the correct French form.
data.expectedOutcome: Correct singular/plural French and Spanish strings displayed based on the item count passed to Localizer.Plural().

items.text: Each .po file has a valid header with Language and charset
items.hint: Check the msgid "" header block at the top of the file

items.text: PO files are placed next to the controller or view they localize
Every msgid exactly matches the string passed to _localizer["..."]
items.hint: Keys are case-sensitive and must match exactly

items.text: Plural entries use msgid_plural with indexed msgstr[n]
items.hint: msgstr[0] = n=0, msgstr[1] = n>0 for French

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: PO files are plain-text gettext format files — no compilation, easy for translators.
Install OrchardCore.Localization.Core and call AddPortableObjectLocalization() in Program.cs.
Each .po file covers one culture and lives next to the controller or view it localizes.
Use msgid_plural with indexed msgstr[n] entries for pluralization.
Use msgctxt to scope the same string to different translations in different views.
IStringLocalizer and IViewLocalizer work identically with .po and .resx files.
data.takeaway: PO files shine when working with translators or needing pluralization. They are the standard choice for open-source and enterprise localization workflows.

items.question: Do I need both AddViewLocalization and AddPortableObjectLocalization?
items.answer: Yes. AddViewLocalization enables the IViewLocalizer service itself. AddPortableObjectLocalization tells ASP.NET Core to use .po files instead of .resx when resolving localized strings.

items.question: Can I mix .resx and .po files in the same project?
items.answer: No. AddPortableObjectLocalization() globally switches the localization system to PO files. If you need both, you would need to manage them separately or stick with one format.

items.question: What does 'gettext' have to do with ASP.NET Core?
items.answer: Gettext is a standard C internationalization library. The PO format it uses is widely supported by translation tools. OrchardCore.Localization.Core brings that format to ASP.NET Core.

items.question: How many plural forms does my language need?
items.answer: Use Poedit or the gettext plural formula to determine this. French and Spanish need 2 forms. English needs 2. Arabic needs 6. The header in the .po file declares the formula.
